generalInstructions: Answer the following questions from Group-A, B and C as directed.
Group A has three sections: Q1 MCQs, Q2 fill in the blanks, and Q3 short answers. Answer any ten from each section: 1 × 10 = 10 per section.
Group B: answer any six questions, 2 × 6 = 12.
Group C: answer any one alternative from each of Q5, Q6 and Q7, 6 × 1 = 6 per set.

groups.title: Group A — Objective and short answer
groups.instruction: Q1 choose the correct alternative, Q2 fill in the blanks, Q3 answer in brief. Answer any ten from each section: 1 × 10 = 10 per section.
groups.additionalInstruction: Three independent ten-mark sections; 30 marks total.
groups.markSplit: 1 mark per item; 10 from each section

groups.title: Group C — Long answer
groups.instruction: Answer any one alternative from each of Q5, Q6 and Q7: 6 × 1 = 6 per set.
groups.additionalInstruction: Three independent choice sets; 18 marks total.

questions.question: The number of successful accesses to memory stated as a fraction is called ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) Hit rate.**

questions.question: The final addition sum of `0110` and `0110` is ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer: A) 1101.** Binary addition actually gives `1100`; the printed options contain no exact match.
questions.sourceNote: Legacy answer chose A as the closest option; standard binary sum is `1100`.

questions.question: What does CSA stand for?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) Carry Save Addition.**

questions.question: Individual control word of the micro routine is called a ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) Micro instruction.**

questions.question: Which circuit converts binary data into decimal?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Decoder** among the printed options.

questions.question: The situation wherein the data of operands are not available is called ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Data hazard.**

questions.question: What is the full form of CISC?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) Complex Instruction Set Computer.**

questions.question: The alternate way of writing `ADD #5,R1` is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) `ADDI 5,R1;`** among the printed options.

questions.question: In order to read multiple bytes of a row at the same time, we make use of ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Memory extension.**
questions.sourceNote: The identical March 2023 CSO question used A; legacy June answer B is corrected.

questions.question: In a full adder the sum circuit is implemented using ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) XOR.**

questions.question: Computer address bus is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Unidirectional.**

questions.question: Which computer bus connects the CPU to memory on the system board?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) System bus.**

questions.question: The instructions used for reading an input port and writing an output port respectively are ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) IN, OUT.**

questions.question: Micro operation is shown as ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) R1 ← R2.**

questions.question: An interrupt that can be temporarily ignored is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) Maskable interrupt.**

questions.question: ______ is used to store data, instructions and results permanently for future use.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** secondary/auxiliary memory.

questions.question: ______ is generally used to increase the apparent size of physical memory.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** virtual memory.

questions.question: Gray Code is also called ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** reflected binary code.

questions.question: Instruction register stores ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** the currently fetched instruction.

questions.question: A high speed memory placed between the CPU and primary memory is known as ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** cache memory.

questions.question: I/O address in 8086 is ______ bit.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** 16-bit.

questions.question: Techniques that automatically move programs and data blocks into physical memory when required are called ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** demand paging / virtual memory.

questions.question: Hit ratio is maximum in ______ mapping.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** fully associative mapping.

questions.question: The bias value for single-precision floating point numbers is ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** 127.

questions.question: `MOV AX, [2A50]` is an example of ______ addressing mode.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** direct addressing mode.

questions.question: Loop unrolling is a technique to improve ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** instruction-level parallelism / execution speed.

questions.question: Page table resides in ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** main memory.

questions.question: Microinstruction consists of ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** control-field bits and next-address/sequencing information.

questions.question: The smallest entity of memory is called ______.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** a bit / memory cell.

questions.question: A source program is usually in ______ language.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** high-level language.

questions.question: How does the control unit control other units?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** It generates timing and control signals that coordinate fetch, decode, execute, and data movement.

questions.question: Give an example of a 4-bit, 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit microprocessor.
What is Bus?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A shared set of address, data, and control lines.

questions.question: What is MAR and MDR?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Memory Address Register and Memory Data/Buffer Register.

questions.question: What is register?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A small, fast CPU storage location.

questions.question: What is interrupt?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A signal that temporarily diverts the CPU to a service routine.

questions.question: What is non-volatile memory?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Memory that retains data without power, e.g. ROM/flash.

questions.question: What is logical address?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** The address generated by the CPU before translation to a physical address.

questions.question: Which is an error-detecting code?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Parity bit (also checksum/CRC).

questions.question: What is the logic shift?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A bit shift that inserts zeros.

questions.question: What type of device converts digital signal into a form intelligible to the user?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** An output device / D-A converter or display interface.

questions.question: Which memory stores the instruction required to start a computer?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** ROM / firmware (BIOS).

questions.question: Define clock rate.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** The number of clock cycles per second, measured in Hz.

questions.question: What is the RAID system?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Redundant Array of Independent Disks combining disks for performance and/or redundancy.

questions.question: What are the three main elements of the control unit?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Instruction/decoder logic, timing/control-signal generator, and sequencing/next-state logic.

questions.question: What is Cache memory?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A small fast SRAM between CPU and main memory.

questions.question: What is control memory address?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** The address of the next microinstruction in control store.

questions.question: What is the 2's complement representation of -6?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** In 8 bits, `11111010`.

questions.question: What is clock signal in COA?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** A periodic signal synchronizing CPU operations.

questions.question: Is USB a bus?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** It is a serial bus/interface standard.

questions.question: Draw the block diagram of the half adder.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Two inputs A/B feed XOR for Sum and AND for Carry.

questions.question: Draw a multiplication circuit diagram.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Shift-and-add multiplier using partial-product AND gates, adders, and registers.

questions.question: What's the difference between interrupt service routine and subroutine?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** ISR is triggered asynchronously by hardware and saves context; a subroutine is called explicitly by program control.

questions.question: What do you mean by the write-back policy?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Update cache only and write the block to main memory when it is replaced.

questions.question: What is RISC Pipeline?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Overlapping fetch, decode, execute, memory, and write-back stages for simple RISC instructions.

questions.question: What size of MUXs are needed?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Insufficient context in the scan; a 2-to-1 MUX is the common one-bit selection element.
questions.sourceNote: The scan does not provide the referenced circuit; model answer is explicitly uncertain.

questions.question: Explain the components of the Computer system and what is micro operation?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** CPU, memory, I/O, and buses; a micro-operation is an elementary register transfer.

questions.question: Represent `(12.625)₁₀` in 32-bit floating point representation and what is odd parity checker?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** IEEE-754 single precision `0 10000010 10010100000000000000000`; odd parity checker verifies an odd number of 1 bits.

questions.question: Describe the Von-Neumann Architecture with diagram? Explain the Bus Structure with examples.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Shared memory for instructions/data, CPU with ALU/control/registers, I/O, and address/data/control buses.

questions.question: Describe the Flag Register of 8086 microprocessor.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** 16-bit FLAGS with CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF, OF and status/control bits.

questions.question: Perform multiplication between 23 and 17 using fixed point multiplication algorithm.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Shift-and-add partial products; result `391`.

questions.question: What are the key characteristics of micro-programmed control? Explain different types of micro operation.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Control store, microinstructions, easy modification; register-transfer, arithmetic, logic, shift, and memory/I/O micro-operations.

questions.question: Discuss the various mapping techniques used in cache memory.
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Direct, fully associative, and set-associative mapping.

questions.question: What is virtual memory? How does it work?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** It maps logical addresses to physical frames and swaps pages between RAM and disk on demand.

questions.question: How can you interface RAM and ROM EPROM to microprocessor 8086? What is the use of EPROM?
questions.answer: **Model answer:** Decode address ranges and connect data/control/address buses; EPROM stores firmware/BIOS and is erasable by UV light.
